Incubating at a stable water temperature of 27.6 °C [T = 27.6 °C], the embryonated eggs undergo rapid development, with chorion rupture and larval eclosion occurring after just 3.6 days [ab = 3.6 days]. This brief embryonic period is characteristic of many tropical labrids that spawn in warm, oligotrophic waters where rapid hatching may reduce vulnerability to egg predators. Following eclosion, the yolk-sac larva enters a brief lecithotrophic phase, relying entirely on endogenous yolk reserves before the onset of exogenous feeding. The transition to planktivory marks a critical bottleneck, as first prey capture must occur before complete yolk absorption to avoid the point of no return.

As the pelagic larvae grow, they undergo a pronounced morphological transformation during larval metamorphosis, culminating in benthic settlement onto coral reefs. At the point of juvenile recruitment, individuals have attained a body plan that closely resembles the adult form. The species displays a characteristic growth trajectory, with field studies estimating that the ultimate total length reaches 27 centimeters [Li = 27 centimeters] in fully grown adults. Growth rates are strongly influenced by food availability and water temperature, with the warm 27.6 °C [T = 27.6 °C] conditions typical of its Indo-Pacific habitat supporting continuous year-round development. Juveniles can be observed actively foraging on small crustaceans and polychaetes shortly after settlement, building the somatic mass necessary for the eventual transition to sexual maturity.

The onset of gonadal activity in Halichoeres hortulanus occurs at a specific size threshold. Analysis of captured specimens indicates that the total length at puberty is 12.8 centimeters [Lp = 12.8 centimeters], a measurement that corresponds to the size at which individuals begin to exhibit mature gametes. The gonadosomatic index (GSI) has been recorded at approximately 10% [GSI = approximately 10%] under the stable thermal conditions of 27.6 °C [T = 27.6 °C]. This value, while derived from comparative data on the related wrasse Centrolabrus exoletus, suggests a moderate allocation of body mass to gamete production. Individuals continue to accumulate somatic tissue even after reaching maturity, with the ultimate wet weight of fully grown fish reaching approximately 247 grams [Wwi = approximately 247 grams], a substantial increase from the weight recorded at the onset of puberty.

The timing of key life history events is tightly coupled to environmental temperature. Once this size is attained, fish can participate in the daily spawning aggregations that characterize the reproductive period. Mortality rates are highest during the larval phase, with predation and starvation accounting for substantial losses before the pelagic-benthic transition. The ultimate total length of 27 centimeters [Li = 27 centimeters] places it among the smaller-bodied terminal males in the genus Halichoeres, a group known for protogynous hermaphroditism.
